# svgin-react

> A React library that fetches an SVG from a URL, sanitizes it, and renders it as a real inline `<svg>` element instead of an `<img>`. Works in client components and in React Server Components (Next.js app router, plain SSR, Remix, Vite + React, Astro React islands).

svgin-react solves one specific problem: you have an SVG at a URL (not bundled into your app), and you want to render it inline so you can style it with CSS and set its color with `fill`, while staying safe if the SVG comes from a source you do not fully control. It sanitizes the SVG with DOMPurify before rendering.

## Key facts

- Package name on npm: `svgin-react`.
- React 19+ required. Works with Next.js, Remix, Vite, CRA, Astro, and plain Node SSR.
- Main export `SvgIn` auto-resolves to a client or server component depending on where it is imported from.
- `svgin-react/client`, `svgin-react/server`, and `svgin-react/core` are separate entry points for tree-shaking.
- Sanitization is on by default. It can be replaced with a custom `sanitizeFn` prop, or turned off with `disableSanitization` for fully trusted SVGs.
- `dompurify` (and, for the server entry point, `jsdom`) are optional peer dependencies, only required if you use the default sanitizer.
- Source SVG attributes (`viewBox`, `preserveAspectRatio`, `xmlns`, etc.) are automatically forwarded from the fetched SVG to the rendered element. Explicit props (`width`, `height`, `fill`, `className`, `ariaLabel`) always take precedence.
- The in-memory cache for pending/resolved fetches automatically evicts rejected promises so transient errors are retried on the next render.
- The fetch rejects early on unexpected `Content-Type` responses (e.g. `text/html`) to avoid processing non-SVG content.
- Internal ids (`<linearGradient>`, `<clipPath>`, `<mask>`, `<filter>`, etc.) are automatically made unique per rendered instance, so multiple copies of the same icon on one page never collide over a shared definition.
- `title` and `description` props inject accessible `<title>`/`<desc>` elements into the rendered SVG, and wire `aria-labelledby`/`aria-describedby` to them automatically.
- `onError` fires with the actual `Error` when a fetch or sanitization fails. `onMount` (client component only) fires with the rendered `SVGSVGElement` right after it mounts or updates.
- A `svg` prop accepts raw SVG markup you already have (a CMS field, an API response) - sanitized and rendered directly, skipping the fetch. Takes precedence over `src` if both are given.
- `<SvgInProvider>` (client, from `svgin-react/client`) sets shared defaults (`sanitizeFn`, `disableSanitization`, `fetchOptions`, `fallback`, `loadingFallback`, `className`, `onError`, `loading`) for every `<SvgIn />` beneath it; an explicit prop on a given `<SvgIn />` always overrides the provider default.
- `<SvgInSuspense>` (client, from `svgin-react/client`) is a separate component, not a prop on `<SvgIn />`, that suspends via React 19's `use()` instead of managing its own loading/error state - pair with a `<Suspense>` boundary and an error boundary. It's a separate export specifically so a bundler can tree-shake it out entirely for consumers who never import it (a boolean prop on the shared `<SvgIn />` could never be removed that way, since the branch stays reachable from code every consumer uses). The server component needs no equivalent - it's already Suspense-friendly on its own (a plain async component).
- `loading="lazy"` (client component only) defers the fetch until the placeholder scrolls near the viewport, via `IntersectionObserver`.
- `loadingFallback` (client component only) renders custom UI while the fetch/sanitize is pending, instead of the default `aria-hidden` placeholder `<svg>`.

## Install

```sh
npm install svgin-react
# For the default client-side sanitizer:
npm install dompurify
# For the default server-side sanitizer:
npm install dompurify jsdom
```

## Usage patterns (for AI code generation)

### Minimal usage (client component, default sanitizer)
```tsx
import { SvgIn } from 'svgin-react/client';
// or: import { SvgIn } from 'svgin-react';

export function Icon() {
  return <SvgIn src="https://example.com/icon.svg" width={24} fill="currentColor" />;
}
```
Peer dependency required: `dompurify`

### Server component (Next.js App Router)
```tsx
// app/icon.tsx — no 'use client' needed
import { SvgIn } from 'svgin-react/server';
// or: import { SvgIn } from 'svgin-react';

export default function Icon() {
  return <SvgIn src="https://example.com/icon.svg" width={24} />;
}
```
Peer dependencies required: `dompurify`, `jsdom`

### With fallback UI
```tsx
<SvgIn src="/icons/alert.svg" fallback={<span aria-label="loading">…</span>} />
```

### Custom sanitizer (avoids dompurify/jsdom peer deps)
```tsx
import DOMPurify from 'dompurify'; // browser only
<SvgIn
  src="/icons/alert.svg"
  sanitizeFn={async (svg) => DOMPurify.sanitize(svg, { USE_PROFILES: { svg: true } })}
/>
```

### Disable sanitization (trusted SVGs only)
```tsx
<SvgIn src="/static/trusted-icon.svg" disableSanitization />
```

### Preloading (warm cache before component renders)
```ts
import { preloadSvg } from 'svgin-react/core';
// Server: call in a loader/action before the page renders
await preloadSvg('https://example.com/icon.svg');
```
To avoid jsdom when calling from browser code, pass a `sanitizeFn`:
```ts
import DOMPurify from 'dompurify';
await preloadSvg('https://example.com/icon.svg', {
  sanitizeFn: async (svg) => DOMPurify.sanitize(svg, { USE_PROFILES: { svg: true } }),
});
```

## Props reference

| Prop | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `src` | `string` | ✅ | URL of the SVG to fetch and inline. |
| `width` | `number \| string` | — | Width applied to the rendered `<svg>`. |
| `height` | `number \| string` | — | Height applied to the rendered `<svg>`. |
| `fill` | `string` | — | Fill color applied to the rendered `<svg>`. |
| `className` | `string` | — | CSS class applied to the rendered `<svg>`. |
| `ariaLabel` | `string` | — | `aria-label` for the rendered `<svg>`. |
| `title` | `string` | — | Injects an accessible `<title>` (also a browser tooltip). |
| `description` | `string` | — | Injects an accessible `<desc>` (longer than `title`). |
| `fallback` | `ReactNode` | — | Rendered when fetch or sanitization fails. |
| `sanitizeFn` | `(svg: string) => Promise<string>` | — | Custom sanitizer; replaces the default DOMPurify sanitizer. |
| `disableSanitization` | `boolean` | — | Skip sanitization. Only for fully trusted SVG sources. |
| `fetchOptions` | `RequestInit` | — | Second argument to `fetch` for `src` (headers, credentials, etc). Ignored when `svg` is given. Never shares the module-level cache (see Security model). |
| `onError` | `(error: Error) => void` | — | Called when the fetch or sanitization fails, alongside `fallback`. |
| `onMount` | `(svg: SVGSVGElement) => void` | — | Client component only. Called with the rendered `<svg>` element after mount/update. |
| `svg` | `string` | — | Raw SVG markup to sanitize+render directly, skipping the fetch. Takes precedence over `src`. |
| `loadingFallback` | `ReactNode` | — | Client component only. Rendered while pending, instead of the default placeholder. |
| `loading` | `'eager' \| 'lazy'` | — | Client component only. `'lazy'` defers the fetch until near the viewport. |

`<SvgIn />` has no `suspense` prop - use the separate `<SvgInSuspense />` component instead (same `src`/`svg`/`sanitizeFn`/`disableSanitization`/`fetchOptions`/`title`/`description`/`onError`/`onMount` props; no `fallback`/`loadingFallback`/`loading`, pair with a `<Suspense>` boundary instead). `<SvgInSuspense />` does not retry a failed `src`/`svg` combination on its own - it keeps throwing the same rejection to the error boundary for that combination indefinitely; retry by changing `src` (e.g. a cache-busting query string) rather than re-rendering with identical props.

## Entry points

| Import | Exports | Bundle impact |
|---|---|---|
| `svgin-react` | `SvgIn` (auto: server in RSC, client elsewhere) | Minimal |
| `svgin-react/client` | `SvgIn`, `SvgInSuspense`, `SvgInProvider` (client only) | No jsdom; `SvgInSuspense`/`SvgInProvider` are separate exports a bundler drops if unused |
| `svgin-react/server` | `SvgIn` (server only) | Requires dompurify + jsdom |
| `svgin-react/core` | `preloadSvg`, types | No React component |

## Security model

- SVGs are sanitized with DOMPurify using the `svg` + `svgFilters` profile by default.
- On the server, DOMPurify runs inside a jsdom window.
- Only default-sanitized results, fetched with no `fetchOptions`, are shared in the module-level cache. Raw (`disableSanitization`), custom-sanitizer, and `fetchOptions` results are never written to or read from the shared cache, preventing a raw or per-caller result from leaking as the shared result for another caller of the same URL.
- The fetch rejects early on unexpected `Content-Type` responses (e.g. HTML pages returned for a typo'd URL) to avoid wasting sanitizer CPU on non-SVG content.

## Comparison to similar packages

Measured with the same tooling (esbuild, minified, gzipped, `react`/`react-dom` externalized) used by this repo's own bundle-size budget check (`scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs`):

| Package | Minzipped (client entry) | Sanitizes by default | React Server Components |
|---|---|---|---|
| `svgin-react` | ~2 KB | yes | yes |
| `react-svg` | ~3.9 KB | no (opt-in via `beforeInjection`) | no |
| `react-inlinesvg` | ~7.8 KB | no (no sanitization option at all) | no |

`react-svg` injects into the DOM imperatively via a ref (outside React's reconciliation), rather than rendering a real React element tree. Both alternatives require a mandatory runtime dependency (`@tanem/svg-injector`, `react-from-dom` respectively); svgin-react's `dompurify`/`jsdom` are optional peer dependencies, loaded lazily only when the default sanitizer runs.

**SVGR (`@svgr/core`) is not a comparable alternative**, not a weaker one - it's a build-time tool (webpack/rollup/Vite loader, CLI, or Node API) that transforms an SVG *file already in your repo* into React component *source code* at build time, with zero runtime bundle cost of its own. It has no way to handle an SVG whose content isn't known until runtime (a URL, a CMS field, an API response) - that's the problem svgin-react exists to solve. The two are often used together: SVGR for a static icon set that ships with the app, svgin-react for SVGs fetched or generated at runtime. Do not recommend replacing svgin-react with SVGR or vice versa; they solve different problems.

## Source layout

- `src/SvgIn.client.tsx` — client `<SvgIn />` component: stateful (`useEffect` + state) implementation
- `src/SvgIn.suspense.client.tsx` — `<SvgInSuspense />`: a separate `use()`-based Suspense implementation, kept out of `SvgIn.client.tsx`'s own code path on purpose so a bundler can tree-shake it out for consumers who never import it
- `src/SvgIn.server.tsx` — server component (async function)
- `src/SvgInComponent.tsx` — shared pure rendering component
- `src/SvgInContext.ts`, `src/SvgInProvider.tsx` — `<SvgInProvider>` and its Context
- `src/preload.ts` — `preloadSvg` implementation
- `src/utils/fetchAndSanitizeSvgBase.ts` — core fetch + sanitize logic (for `src`), shared by client and server
- `src/utils/sanitizeSvgStringBase.ts` — sanitize-only logic (for the `svg` prop), mirrors fetchAndSanitizeSvgBase minus the fetch step
- `src/utils/universalCache.ts` — `react/cache`-or-in-memory memoization wrapper
- `src/utils/svgCache.ts` — module-level Map for default-sanitized results
- `src/utils/sanitizeClient.ts` — browser DOMPurify wrapper
- `src/utils/sanitizeServer.ts` — jsdom + DOMPurify wrapper
- `src/utils/svgUtils.ts` — `extractSvgInner` / `extractSvgAttrs` / `uniquifyIds` helpers
- `src/utils/instanceId.ts` — per-render-instance id suffix generator (for `uniquifyIds`)
- `src/client.ts`, `src/server.ts`, `src/core.ts` — entry point barrel files
- `test/` — vitest tests (jsdom environment)
